title: Trial-burst kernel sampler with rollback for sequence-length drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe intermittent latency regressions on some model endpoints when incoming sequence length distributions shift (e.g., customers move from short prompts to long-context use). Existing kernel selection heuristics are static per-profile and can be suboptimal during distribution drift.

Goal: Implement a low-overhead, online trial-burst sampling system that periodically and safely trials alternative kernel variants on a tiny fraction of requests (bucketed by model, layer group, and seq-len). If a sampled variant shows statistically significant improvement over the baseline for that bucket, the runtime will promote it; otherwise it will rollback. The system must have strict safety budgets, warmup accounting, and be transparent in telemetry.

Core idea: For each (model-version, hardware-class, seqlen-bucket) tuple maintain a small candidate list of compiled kernel variants. When sampling is triggered, schedule a short burst (N requests or M milliseconds) routed to the candidate variant. Collect microbenchmarks (latency P50/P95, throughput, GPU utilization, token-per-second, memory headroom) and aggregate with warmup-aware smoothing. Decide promotion based on a conservative effect-size threshold and bootstrap confidence to avoid noisy promotions. Provide automatic rollback and manual pinning via Console.

Key constraints and requirements:
- Budgeted sampling: max 0.5% of traffic per tuple by default; configurable per-customer for Dedicated.
- Warmup handling: exclude first K decode tokens or use prefill-only trials for prefill-optimized kernels.
- Safety policy: rollback on any error increase or >5% writer/timeout spike.
- Metrics: per-tuple baseline vs candidate histograms, sample_count, decision_reason, rollback_reason, rollout_history.
- Integration: kernel fingerprint DB, kernel-variant compile cache, routing policy (canary nodes), and Console UI for trial visualization.

Acceptance criteria:
- Trials add <1% median latency overhead on production p50 across sampled percentage when sampling budget set to 0.5%.
- For at least 3 production endpoints with seqlen drift, show >=10% lower cost-per-token after promotion vs baseline in canary runs.
- Rollback triggers correctly on error/latency regressions in >95% of simulated perturbation tests.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Trial-Burst+Kernel+Sampler+Design
- Kernel candidate registry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1445
- Bench harness (internal): https://go.redwood.ai/bench/trial-burst

2026-02-18 - Aisha Patel (PM): Confirmed business priority from customer success: two SMB customers reported doubled p95 after they switched to longer prompts. They allowed a canary on 1% traffic for experiments. Moving to P1.

2026-02-24 - Elena Novak (SRE): Implemented sampling budget enforcement in ingress proxy; added sampling tokens and per-customer limit. Initial canary runs scheduled for runtime-1.21 on canary pool cp-canary-2.

2026-03-02 - Marco Liu: Prototype PR #1445 created for kernel candidate registry and lightweight telemetry tags (candidate_id, tuple_key, sample_id). Microbench results on canary show candidate A reduces decode token latency by ~8% at seqlen 1024 but regresses p95 at seqlen <64. Added bucketed decision logic.

2026-03-04 - Design review notes: - Add statistical significance with bootstrap CI instead of t-test because latency distributions are heavy-tailed. - Define minimum 200 effective samples after warmup for promotion decisions. - Add manual pin override in Console for enterprise customers.

2026-03-05 - Marco Liu: Running fault-injection tests. Observed one case where a candidate produced sporadic OOM on 2/10 trials; added memory headroom check before promotion and blacklist the variant for that tuple.
2026-03-05 - QA note (Ravi Sharma): Need unit/integration tests for sample-budget enforcement, warmup exclusion, and rollback conditions. Added tasks in this ticket checklist.
